idea-plugin.name: Adamantium AUML
idea-plugin.description:
Editing support for AUML, the markup of Adamantium UI (.auml files), with a live preview drawn by the framework itself.

  • Live preview beside or below the markup, rendered from the application's own build in its own theme. It follows edits as you type and plays animations; a click on an element selects it and moves the caret to its line, and Go to Source opens the file a nested view was declared in.
  • Completion, diagnostics, formatting and go to definition from the AUML language server, which knows the types of the project and its packages.
  • Syntax highlighting, folding, and New | AUML File for windows, views, docking panes, themes, style sets, resource dictionaries and the application's blueprint.
  • Language files (.alang), the application's strings in each language: highlighting, completion of keys and formats, the build's checks as you type, a quick fix that adds the strings a translation lacks, and New | Language File for a table or its translation.
  • The project templates for File | New Solution: offered at startup when missing, and installed or updated any time with Tools | Install Adamantium UI Templates.

Requirements: the .NET 10 SDK and a project that references the Adamantium.UI NuGet package. The preview runs the designer that package carries on the project's own build, so build the project once before previewing. LSP4IJ is installed with this plugin.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
New | AUML File offers an Application Blueprint: the application's first window, theme, theme variant, language, resources and style sets in markup, from which the build writes the entry point. A second blueprint in a project is underlined, and its StartupTheme offers only themes.

{ObservableResource} and {ResourceReference} complete resource keys - the project's own and those of its packages and themes - and only those that fit the property: a brush for a Background, a picture for an Image.

An element name is offered only for what markup can create: no automation peers, interfaces, enums, static or abstract classes, attributes or event data.

Reformat Code lays out .auml and language files by the framework's rules: an element per line, indented by level; one attribute on the tag's line, several one per line under the first; a Setter - and a phrase of a language file - on one line; an empty element closed in place; at most one blank line. Values, comments and text are kept as written. A selection reformats the elements written in it.

A type the build would reject is underlined as it is typed, with the build's message: one it would not find, or one of the wrong kind - a resource dictionary given to a StyleInclude - in an attribute, in {x:Type} or in an extension's argument.

A source is offered only what it takes: <StyleInclude Source=""> the style sets, <ResourceLink Source=""> the resource dictionaries - classes in C# and markup files alike, typed by name or in {x:Type}, nested {ResourceLink Source={x:Type ...}} included - and an image's Source or a bitmap's UriSource the pictures of the project and the folders holding them. Any Type-valued attribute (TargetType, EnumType) completes type names in its value.

A file closed or renamed no longer keeps its problems underlined: the server clears them, and opening or closing a language file checks the other open files of its tables again - a renamed base file stopped being reported missing only after a restart.

New | Language File takes a language picked from its list: the dialog judged the language once, while the box was still empty, and kept saying "Not a language" with OK off.

New | AUML File offers a Ribbon Tab, a Ribbon Group and an Empty file - a <Grid> root with the namespaces already declared, to be replaced by any control. A file with any control at its root is a class of its own, which other markup places by name: a ribbon can be split into a file per tab and a file per group.

A type in {x:Type} and a type or member in {x:Static} that the build would not find is underlined while typing, with the build's own message, and painted as unknown.

A type written without a prefix is found the way the build finds it - by its short name: {x:Static RegionNames.} completes the members of a project type, the project's own types are offered bare, and <Thickness>, <CornerRadius> or a project type as an element are no longer reported unknown. clr-namespace:System;assembly=System.Runtime resolves, so <sys:Double> is no longer red.

New | AUML File offers a Docking Pane: one file with a <Pane> root - its title, whether it is a document or a tool, and where it docks - which the build makes a class of its own.
